summary: NAVI is a structurally shrinking student-loan-servicer-turned-portfolio-runoff vehicle with clean audit (KPMG unqualified, NO_GOING_CONCERN), fully resolved $120M CFPB settlement (17 reaffirming filings, zero adverse evolutions), confirmed 85% headcount reduction and on-time exit from all three divestiture transitions (MOHELA outsourcing, healthcare sale, government services sale), and trivial insider selling ($922K over 12 months) — strong universal-quality and disclosure-quality signals. OFFSETS: FY25 GAAP net LOSS $80M (vs $131M income FY24), Q1 2026 recovered to only $17M NI (run-rate ~$68M vs $221M Core Earnings FY24), short-term unsecured maturity wall TRIPLED to $1.2B by Q1 2026 (10-K only flagged $0.5B), Adjusted Tangible Equity Ratio sequentially eroded 10.0% to 8.9% over 15 months, $280M FY25 provision for loan losses against 6.3% Private Education Loan delinquencies, decelerating buyback execution at the trough (33% YoY slower), and most importantly an UNDISCLOSED-IN-10-K CEO succession (turnaround partner Edward Bramson replacing Yowan effective June 5, 2026, announced 7 weeks AFTER the 10-K, with the CFO already replaced in January 2026). Composite 0.750 across 8 scored claims (3 PASS / 4 MODERATE / 1 SEVERE / 0 RED / 0 UNVERIFIABLE). The SEVERE flag is the leadership transition omission: a turnaround-firm-partner CEO arriving 'for Phase 2' is a material narrative discontinuity that the 10-K should have foreshadowed.
